title: Biological/Cultural Controls, Thresholds & Resistance Management
level: Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Learners progressing through the Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist pathway
Cultivation personnel responsible for IPM program design, biological/cultural control integration, monitoring thresholds and resistance-management handoff
prerequisites: Arthropod Pest Biology, Identification & IPM and Plant Disease, HLVd & Biosecurity or equivalent advanced plant-health foundation
evidencePolicy: Control-strategy claims are grounded in cannabis-specific integrated disease/IPM literature, university greenhouse IPM guidance and technical resistance-management guidance. Universal cannabis action thresholds, pesticide product recommendations and off-label use are explicitly excluded.
assessmentPolicy: The dedicated specialist assessment is development-only until exact-version technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize pesticide selection/application or override label, jurisdiction, licensing or facility controls.
description: Develops specialist IPM decision-making across preventive, cultural, mechanical, biological and chemical-control contexts, with emphasis on threshold logic, beneficial-organism compatibility, resistance stewardship, post-intervention verification and documented decision boundaries.
learningOutcomes: Use representative monitoring, crop impact and facility decision rules to distinguish observation thresholds, action thresholds and treatment authority without inventing universal cannabis pest-count triggers.
Compare biological, cultural, mechanical and environmental control tactics by target pest/pathogen, life stage, timing, compatibility, expected response and verification needs.
Evaluate beneficial-organism compatibility with sanitation, environmental conditions and other interventions while recognizing that no single control tactic is universally effective.
Apply resistance-management principles by distinguishing mode of action from brand identity, avoiding repeated selection pressure and preserving label/local-authority boundaries.
Build an IPM decision and follow-up record that links evidence, chosen tactic, authorization, compatibility checks, monitoring method, response criteria and escalation/closure decisions.
